items.stem: The following statement about basic concepts of national income accounting is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The value of intermediate goods is added separately to GDP."
items.answer: It is already included in the value of final goods, so adding it again would be double counting.

items.stem: 'Machines purchased are always final goods.' Do you agree? Explain.
items.answer: Machines bought by a firm for use in production are capital goods, which are final goods as they are not transformed or resold in that year; but a machine bought by a dealer for resale is an intermediate good; so classification depends on end use.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Machines bought by a firm for use in production are capital goods, which are final goods as they are not transformed or resold in that year; but a machine bought by a dealer for resale is an intermediate good; so classification depends on end use.

items.stem: "Net investment can be smaller than gross investment." Examine this statement with reference to basic concepts of national income accounting.

items.stem:

(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Net investment can be smaller than gross investment. (1)

items.answer: (i) The wear and tear of fixed capital during production, also called consumption of fixed capital. (ii) A part of gross investment only replaces the fixed capital used up through depreciation. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Net investment is gross investment minus depreciation.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The wear and tear of fixed capital during production, also called consumption of fixed capital. (ii) A part of gross investment only replaces the fixed capital used up through depreciation. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Net investment is gross investment minus depreciation.

items.stem:
From the following data about a printing press, calculate net value added at factor cost (NVAFC):
Depreciation: ₹35 crore
Intermediate consumption: ₹2,085 crore
Change in stock: ₹120 crore
Net indirect taxes: ₹15 crore
Sales: ₹4,740 crore
items.answer: NVAFC = ₹2,725 crore
items.markingKey: Value of output = sales + change in stock = 4740 + (120) = 4860; GVAMP = 4860 − 2085 = 2775; NVAFC = GVAMP − depreciation − NIT = 2775 − 35 − 15 = ₹2,725 crore. (1 mark value of output, 1 mark GVAMP, 1 mark NVAFC.)

items.stem:
Calculate national income (NNPFC) by the expenditure method from the following data:
Net indirect taxes: ₹120 crore
Private final consumption expenditure: ₹7,000 crore
Consumption of fixed capital: ₹570 crore
Net factor income from abroad: −₹115 crore
Government final consumption expenditure: ₹1,050 crore
Gross domestic capital formation: ₹1,725 crore
Net exports: ₹135 crore
items.answer: National income = ₹9,105 crore
items.markingKey: GDPMP = PFCE + GFCE + GDCF + net exports = 7000 + 1050 + 1725 + (135) = 9910 (2 marks); NNPFC = GDPMP − depreciation + NFIA − NIT = 9910 − 570 + (−115) − 120 = ₹9,105 crore (2 marks).

items.stem:
From the following data, calculate (i) net domestic product at factor cost and (ii) gross national product at market price:
Rent: ₹300 crore
Profit: ₹710 crore
Mixed income of self-employed: ₹870 crore
Net indirect taxes: ₹310 crore
Interest: ₹290 crore
Net factor income from abroad: ₹65 crore
Consumption of fixed capital: ₹100 crore
Compensation of employees: ₹5,100 crore
items.answer: (i) NDPFC = ₹7,270 crore; (ii) GNPMP = ₹7,745 crore
items.markingKey: (i) NDPFC = COE + rent + interest + profit + mixed income = 5100 + 300 + 290 + 710 + 870 = ₹7,270 crore (2 marks); (ii) GNPMP = NDPFC + depreciation + NFIA + NIT = 7270 + 100 + (65) + 310 = ₹7,745 crore (2 marks).

items.stem: Nominal GDP of an economy was ₹5,800 crore in year 1 and ₹7,308 crore in year 2. The GDP deflator was 100 in year 1 and 120 in year 2. Calculate real GDP in both years and the growth rate of real GDP. Did the economy's output really grow as much as nominal GDP suggests?
